Expand your access with a residence permit

If your Australian passport has limited reach, a residence permit can unlock many additional destinations. Pairing your passport with one of the permits below typically adds 5–15 new visa-free or visa-on-arrival countries:

  • UAE residence permit — strong for South Asian passport holders, unlocks Armenia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Serbia
  • US Green Card — unlocks Mexico, Canada (via eTA), several Caribbean and Central American countries
  • Schengen residence permit — unlocks Turkey, Balkans, several visa-free short stays across the EU

Frequently asked questions

How many countries can Australian passport holders visit visa-free?
Australian passport holders have visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to approximately 144 countries — 110 visa-free and 34 visa-on-arrival. Notable visa-free destinations include Albania, Andorra, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Armenia.
Is the Australian passport strong?
Yes — the Australian passport is considered strong, giving access to 144+ destinations without needing to arrange a visa in advance.
Do I need an ETA or e-visa for some countries?
Yes. 40 destinations require an e-visa (online application before arrival) for Australian passport holders. These are typically quicker than embassy visas but still need to be arranged before travel.
Which countries require a full visa in advance?
14 countries require Australian passport holders to obtain a visa from an embassy before travelling. Check the destination embassy's website for specific requirements and processing times.
Can a residence permit or second visa unlock extra countries?
Yes — several residence permits grant bonus visa-free access regardless of your Australian passport. See our guides for UAE residence, US Green Card, and Schengen residence permit to learn which countries unlock for each.
How accurate is this list?
Entries marked with a ✓ badge have been re-verified against an official government source (embassy, ministry, or visa portal) and link to that source. Entries without the badge come from the community-maintained open-source Passport Index Dataset — a reasonable starting point but not individually verified. Rules change frequently. Always confirm with the destination embassy before booking travel.
